capitals.note: 'In 702 Wu Zetian set up the Beiting Protectorate in Ting Prefecture'. The coordinates are those of Beshbalik (near Jimsar), the Tang Ting Prefecture, the researcher's reading.

correction.text: Ting Prefecture (Beiting, Beshbalik) with Yi Prefecture (Hami) and Xi Prefecture (Turfan): Dzungaria, Hami and Turfan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 702 Wu Zetian set up the Beiting Protectorate in Ting Prefecture' and 'granted it governorship over Yi Prefecture'; it also governed Xi Prefecture. The pages name the three prefectures but no frontier, and the Beiting page gives no area; Dzungaria plus Turfan-Hami is the researcher's reading and probably over-wide on the north. From 764 'cutting off the Anxi and Beiting protectorates from the Tang dynasty' the shape stands only on paper.

correction.text: Ting Prefecture (Beiting, Beshbalik) with Yi Prefecture (Hami) and Xi Prefecture (Turfan): Dzungaria, Hami and Turfan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the last year. 'In 790 A.D, Tibet occupied the four towns in Anxi and Beiting in the west' (Sino-Tibetan relations page); the Anxi page gives 'by 790' for the last vestiges. The shape is the same; the dissolve event ends it.

ledger.note: 702: the Beiting Protectorate is founded. 'In 702 Wu Zetian set up the Beiting Protectorate in Ting Prefecture' and 'granted it governorship over Yi Prefecture'; Xi Prefecture also fell to it, so Dzungaria, Hami and Turfan leave the Anxi (the Anxi dossier's 702 split).

region.text: Ting Prefecture (Beiting, Beshbalik) with Yi Prefecture (Hami) and Xi Prefecture (Turfan): Dzungaria, Hami and Turfan

ledger.note: 790: Tibet takes Beiting. 'In 790 A.D, Tibet occupied the four towns in Anxi and Beiting in the west'; the Anxi page agrees that 'the last vestiges of the protectorate and its garrisons were defeated by Tibetan forces by 790'. In 764 the Tibetan seizure of Liangzhou had cut it off from the Tang.

wars.name: Tibetan conquest of Beiting

zones.text: Ting Prefecture (Beiting, Beshbalik) with Yi Prefecture (Hami) and Xi Prefecture (Turfan): Dzungaria, Hami and Turfan

wars.outcome: Tibet conquered Liangzhou in 764, cutting off the Anxi and Beiting protectorates, and occupied Beiting in 790.
wars.note: No page opened dates the siege or battle of Beiting itself; the Uyghur-Tibetan fighting of 789-792 is not on the pages read.

certainty.note: Three prefectures named, no frontier on any page; steppe and desert edges are approximate.

notes: Written for ea-04-x on the Andong protectorate's pattern (type colony). The Beiting Protectorate article is a stub, so everything rests on the Anxi page (702, 764) and the Sino-Tibetan relations page (790). Not on any page opened: the 742 Beiting Jiedushi, Beiting's relations with the Uyghurs (the Uyghur-Tibetan fight for Beiting in 789-792), the fate of Xizhou after 790 (Qocho/Uyghur) and the northern extent of Ting Prefecture; the Tang dossier has the same land as a 790 loss to the Tibetans. Beshbalik is a gazetteer place (used as a capital coordinate only); Dzungaria and Turfan-Hami are regions.
